title: SAML 2.0 Setup Wizard: Metadata Exchange Inspector & Validation Heuristics
creator: Asha Patel
description: Add a 'Metadata Exchange Inspector' step to the SAML 2.0 setup wizard. The inspector will fetch IdP metadata from a provided URL or uploaded XML, run a battery of deterministic checks, and present a concise pass/warn/fail dashboard for operators. This ticket covers engineering work for fetching, normalizing, validating certificates, computing fingerprints, detecting entityID collisions, integrating results with the audit log, and wiring RBAC v2 controls so only authorized admins can accept 'warn' states. The goal is to reduce support load from malformed IdP configurations and provide clear remediation suggestions for common operator mistakes.
acceptance_criteria: Wizard includes a distinct 'Metadata Exchange Inspector' step that can be reached after entering basic SSO settings
Inspector can fetch a remote metadata URL with timeouts and retry (configurable), and accept uploaded XML by drag/drop
System produces a human-readable validation summary with explicit categories: syntax, signature, cert-validity, entity-id-uniqueness, endpoint-normalization, and certificate-thumbprint-match
Validation results and the canonicalized metadata blob are recorded to the audit log with metadata_hash (sha256), operator identifier, IP, and outcome
RBAC v2 enforces that only users with 'sso.admin' or higher can bypass 'warn' results; others are blocked from saving until an admin acknowledges
When a certificate is expiring within 30 days the inspector surfaces a clear advisory, includes cert expiration date, and suggests rotation steps
Automated integration tests cover: remote fetch, uploaded XML, expired cert, unsigned metadata, mismatched thumbprint, entityID collision
UI shows an inline 'Apply suggested fixes' where possible (e.g., normalize protocol-relative ACS URLs) and creates a changelist for operator review
All validation outcomes map to deterministic error codes for telemetry and support troubleshooting (see implementation_notes)
implementation_notes: Fetch: use existing http-client with connection pool, set per-fetch timeout 6s, retries 2 with exponential backoff
Normalization: remove insignificant whitespace, sort XML attributes, normalize URLs (add https when missing scheme), and canonicalize XML before hashing

Signature verification: support both embedded signingKey and direct certificate entries; verify signature on EntityDescriptor when present. For unsigned metadata produce WARN rather than FAIL unless tenant policy requires strict signatures
Fingerprinting: compute both SHA1 and SHA256 fingerprints for backward-compat checks; store sha256 in audit index and show both in UI
EntityID collision: query internal identity registry table for other tenants with same entityID. If collision found show blocking FAIL and provide a suggested unique entityID suffix
Certificate rotation: detect overlapping cert validity windows; if new cert shares public key with current but different subject, offer rotation guidance and a dry-run validation
RBAC: check 'sso.admin' scope using RBAC v2 middleware; 'sso.operator' can run inspector but cannot accept 'warn' paths
Audit log schema: record event_type 'saml.metadata.inspect', metadata_hash_sha256, validation_outcome, operator_id, client_ip, idp_entity_id_hint, and optional failure_reasons list
Telemetry: emit metric saml.inspector.fetch_ms, saml.inspector.validation_fail_count, and saml.inspector.warn_accept_count (with tenant tag)
Backward compatibility: keep the previous non-inspector path for existing tenants until feature flag 'saml.inspector-rollout' reaches 100%
milestones: Spike: implement canonicalization + signature verification prototype (2026-03-04)
Core: integrate inspector into wizard UI with fetch/upload and basic checks (2026-03-10)
QA & integration tests, audit log hookup (2026-03-18)
Ship behind feature flag and run limited pilot with 5 enterprise customers (2026-03-22)
risks: Some legacy IdPs publish non-standard metadata that will fail strict validation — we must avoid breaking existing customers and provide a clear opt-in for strict enforcement
Remote fetches can amplify network load or be used for SSRF. Ensure fetcher only follows configured allowlist and validates response content-type and size limits
Storing canonicalized metadata increases storage and retention cost; ensure we compress and respect retention policy
Certificate parsing edge cases (weird encodings) may cause library-level panics; wrap all parsers with defensive guards and circuit breakers
qa_plan: Unit tests for xml canonicalization and fingerprint calculation
Contract tests for signature verification using curated test vectors (valid, tampered, expired)
End-to-end test against a test IdP that returns: well-formed signed metadata, unsigned metadata, expired certs, and duplicate entityID
Manual test: create SSO config as sso.operator and verify blocking when encountering FAIL, then escalate as sso.admin to accept WARN path
Security test: SSRF attempt using metadata URL with internal IPs; ensure fetcher blocks according to allowlist
Audit validation: perform actions and confirm audit events are emitted with correct metadata_hash and operator information
